preamble: Insertion of the palatal glide [j], typically before a word-initial front vowel (prothesis). Proto-Slavic word-initial *e- acquired a prothetic j- (*ezero 'lake' > Czech jezero, against Lithuanian ežeras). Romanian pronounces initial e- in personal pronouns and in forms of 'to be' with [j] (el [jel] 'he', este [ˈjeste] 'is').

examples.to: OCS ѥсмь jesmĭ, Old Czech jsem, Serbo-Croatian jèsam, Old Polish jeśm
examples.note: Initial *e- received a prothetic [j]; the Baltic cognate Lithuanian esmì has none.

examples.to: OCS ѥзеро jezero, Czech jezero, Serbo-Croatian jȅzero

examples.note: Initial e- of the personal pronouns is pronounced with a glide that the Latin source lacks.
Forms of 'to be' beginning in e- take the same initial [j]; eu /jew/ 'I' also shows it.
